nodes.statement: Our aim is to generate more time series at the same grid points of the sample paths of that are distributionally as close to those of as possible.footnoteWhile the original goal was to generate paths following the same distributions of the solution to , the only data available to us are the collection of series in . Hence, to generate new series close to is the best we could do. This is analogous to generating more cat pictures based on a set of existing cat pictures, a typical generative AI (GenAI) task. To do so, we leverage the Markov property of the SDE and train conditional diffusion models to simulate the stochastic increments of . Note that Delta t is not necessarily small in many applications, in which case the resulting stochastic increments of the SDE are generally non-Gaussian. This rules out the method of directly sampling Gaussian increments, a generally easy endeavor even in high dimensions. On the other hand, in high-dimensional settings where d is large, classical density estimation methods such as kernel density estimation become impractical, begging for alternative generative models like ours.

nodes.statement: Instead of using conditional diffusion models to generate SDE paths in a sequential and autoregressive fashion, an alternative approach is to train a single diffusion model to generate samples of the entire trajectory (X(t_1), cdots, X(t_N_T)) directly. In such a case, the dimension of the target distribution is dtimes N_T, which becomes large with a high-dimensional SDE (large d) and/or a large number of observation slots (large N_T). While diffusion models can indeed deal with high-dimensional distributions, they nonetheless require more complex network architectures to train the score functions and longer training times. The autoregressive approach we choose instead reduces the dimension and complexity of the generation task, which allows us to use a simple neural network such as a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for training the conditional score function, leading to a more efficient solution.

Instead of using conditional diffusion models to generate SDE paths in a sequential and autoregressive fashion, an alternative approach is to train a single diffusion model to generate samples of the entire trajectory $(\mathbf{X}(t_1), \cdots, \mathbf{X}(t_{N_T}))$ directly.
In such a case, the dimension of the target distribution is $d\times N_T$, which becomes large with a high-dimensional SDE (large $d$) and/or a large number of observation slots (large $N_T$). While diffusion models can indeed deal with high-dimensional distributions, they nonetheless require more complex network architectures to train the score functions and longer training times. The autoregressive approach we choose instead reduces the dimension and complexity of the generation task, which allows us to use a simple neural network such as a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for training the conditional score function, leading to a more efficient solution.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{prop: path_KL_decomposition}
nodes.statement: Throughout this proof, if a probability distribution is absolutely continuous w.r.t the Lebesgue measure, we simply say this distribution is ACL. We first consider the target paths. For any t_ninT, denote by P_n + 1| n(cdot | x(t_n)) the conditional distribution of X(t_n + 1) given X(t_n) = x(t_n), which is ACL and positive almost everywhere on R^d according to Assumption (b). It follows that the conditional distribution P_DeltaX(t_n; x(t_n)) of the increment is also ACL and positive almost everywhere on R^d. We apply the result of Lemma \ref{lemma: KL_dt}(b) and set $C_{KL} = b$. Note that $\tilde g^2(\tau) = g^2(T_g - \tau) = a(T_g - \tau) + b \ge b$ for any $\tau\in[0, T_g]$. Then, integrating on both sides of \eqref{eq: density_KL_dt_bound} from $\tau_k$ to $\tau_{k + 1}$, we have
\begin{align*}
    &\text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau_{k + 1} | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau_{k + 1} | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}\big) - \lim_{\tau\to\tau_k+}\text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}\big)\\
    &\le \frac{1}{b}\int_{\tau_k}^{\tau_{k + 1}} \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau)\sim\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})} \big\|\tilde f(\tau)\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) - \tilde f(\tau_k)\tilde{\mathbf{z}} + \tilde g^2(\tau)\nabla\log q_{T_g - \tau}(\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau)|\mathbf{c}) -  \tilde g^2(\tau_k)s_\theta(T_g - \tau_k, \tilde{\mathbf{z}}, \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\mathrm{d} \tau\\
    &\qquad + \frac{1}{4b}\int_{\tau_k}^{\tau_{k + 1}} [\tilde g^2(\tau_k) - \tilde g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau)\sim\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log\tilde p_\tau(\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau))\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau.
\end{align*}
Since the above result holds when $\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)= \tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_k) = \tilde {\mathbf{z}}$ for any fixed $\tilde{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we can integrate on both sides of the above inequality w.r.t. $\tilde {\mathbf{z}} = \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)\sim \tilde p_{\tau_k}$. Hence, for the given condition c, there must exist tau_0 such that lambda_tau_0sigma_tau_0^-2 = 2L(c). This allows us to apply Lemma for tau < min\tau_0, tau_k_1\. However, when L(c) is small, tau_0 can be large. To control the magnitude of (the sum of) (tau_k + 1)^6 in Lemma , we introduce a larger Lipschitz constant L_2(c) := L(c) + lambda_min\1,T_g/2\sigma_min\1, T_g/2\^-2. It is clear that nablalog q_0(cdot | c) is also L_2(c)-Lipschitz continuous. We can then define tau_lipz(c) = maxbig\0le taule T_g: lambda_tausigma_tau^-2 ge 2L_2(c)big\. Note that lambda_min\1, T_g/2\sigma_min\1, T_g/2\^-2 le 2L_2(c) and lambda_tausigma_tau^-2 is decreasing in tau. Thus, for any given and fixed condition c, tau_lipz(c) < min\1, T_g/2\ le tau_k_1. Let k_0(c) = min\1le k le K: tau_k ge tau_lipz(c)\le k_1. We can now apply Lemma with settings of s = tau_1, cdots, tau_k_0(c) - 1 and s = tau_lipz(c). nodes.statement: Following , we first consider the stochastic dynamic of the score function big\nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ): tauin[0, T_g)big\ under a given condition c. Recall that the reverse SDE of diffusion models is dtildeY(tau) = [tilde f(tau)tildeY(tau) + tilde g^2(tau) nablalog q_T_g - tau(tilde Y(tau) | c)]dtau + tilde g(tau) dtildeB(tau), where tilde f(tau) := f(T_g - tau) and tilde g(tau) := g(T_g - tau). As in the proof of Lemma 3 of , nablalog q_T_g - tau(cdot | c) is smooth for tauin[0, T_g), and by It\^o's formula we can write dbig[nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big] &= bigg\nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )cdotbig[tilde f(tau)tildeY(tau) + tilde g^2(tau) nablalog q_T_g - tau(tilde Y(tau) | c)big]nonumber\\ & + frac12tilde g^2(tau)cdot Delta big(nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big)bigg\dtau + fracdbig[nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big]d tau d tau nonumber\\ & + tilde g(tau)nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) dtildeB(tau). To further simplify , consider the Fokker–Planck equation for the forward process : d q_tau(y | c) = bigg(-nablacdotbig[(-f(tau)q_tau(y | c)y big] + frac12Deltabig[g^2(tau)q_tau(y|c)big]bigg)dtau, leading to d(log q_tau(y | c)) &= frac1q_tau(y | c)bigg(-nablacdotbig[(-f(tau) q_tau(y | c)ybig] + frac12 Deltabig[g^2(tau)q_tau(y|c)big]bigg)dtau\\ &= bigg(f(tau)d + f(tau)y^Tnablalog q_tau(y | c) + frac12g^2(tau)Deltalog q_tau(y | c) + frac12g^2(tau)\|nablalog q_tau(y | c)\|^2bigg)d tau. It follows that &fracdbig[nablalog q_T_g - tau(y | c )big]d tau = nablafracd(log q_T_g - tau(y | c))d tau \\ &= -bigg(tilde f(tau)nablalog q_T_g - tau(y | c) + tilde f(tau)nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(y | c)cdoty \\ & + frac12tilde g^2(tau)nablabig(Deltalog q_T_g - tau(y | c)big) + tilde g^2(tau)nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(y | c)cdot nablalog q_T_g - tau(y | c)bigg). Substituting into and simplifying, we obtain dbig[nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big] = -tilde f(tau)nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c) d tau + tilde g(tau)nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) dtildeB(tau). Now, we establish the desired bound. First, for fixed s in (0, tau), we have &dbig[(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big] \\ &= -tilde f(tau)(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c) d tau \\ & + tilde g(tau)(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) dtildeB(tau). By Lemma , int_s^tau E_tildeY(u)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - u(tildeY(u))\|^2_Fbig]d u < infty where tildeY(u)sim q_T_g - u(cdot | c), implying that the final term in the above equation is a square-integrable martingale. Integrating on both sides and taking expectations w.r.t. the joint distribution of (tildeY(tau), tildeY(s)) induced by , we get &fracddtauE_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big]\\ &= -E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[tilde f(tau)(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c) big]. Next, if setting tildeLambda(tau) = expbig(int_0^tau tilde f(s)d s big) and applying It\^o's formula to , we obtain dbig[tildeLambda(tau)nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )big] = tildeLambda(tau)tilde g(tau)nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) dtildeB(tau). We know from Lemma that int_s^tautildeLambda^2(u)E_tildeY(u) big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - u(tildeY(u))\|^2_Fbig]d u < infty for any fixed s > 0. By It\^o's isometry and chain rule, we obtain &tildeLambda^2(tau)tilde g^2(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c)\|^2_Fbig]\\ &= fracddtauE_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[\|tildeLambda(tau)nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) - tildeLambda(s)nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )\|^2big] nonumber\\ &= tildeLambda^2(tau)cdot fracddtauE_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2 + 2tilde f(tau)tildeLambda^2(tau) E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2\\ & - 2tildeLambda(tau)tildeLambda(s)cdot fracddtauE_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[(nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )big] \\ & - 2tilde f(tau)tildeLambda(tau)tildeLambda(s)E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[(nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )big]\\ &overset= tildeLambda^2(tau)cdot fracddtauE_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2 + 2tilde f(tau)tildeLambda^2(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2. It follows that & fracddtauE_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2 + 2tilde f(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2\\ &= tilde g^2(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c)\|^2_Fbig]. For any fixed s > 0 and tau > s, and lead to &fracddtauE_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s)) big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )\|^2big]\\ &= fracddtauE_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c )\|^2big] - 2fracddtauE_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[(nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )big]\\ &= tilde g^2(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c)\|^2_Fbig] - 2tilde f(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) ||^2\\ & + 2E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[tilde f(tau)(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c) big]\\ &= tilde g^2(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c)\|^2_Fbig] \\ & - 2tilde f(tau)E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )||^2big]\\ & + 2tilde f(tau)E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s)) big[(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )big]. However, by Young's inequality, &E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[(nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(tau) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(s) | c ))^Tnablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )big]\\ &le frac12bigg[E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s))big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )\|^2big] + E_tildeY(s)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )\|^2big]bigg]. Therefore, we have &fracddtauE_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(s)) big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )\|^2big]\\ &le tilde f(tau)E_tildeY(s)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - s(tildeY(s) | c )\|^2big] + tilde g^2(tau)E_tildeY(tau)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c)\|^2_Fbig]. Let s=tau_k and tauin[tau_k, tau_k + 1]. Integrate both sides of the above equation from tau_k to tau and use Lemma and Lemma to obtain &E_(tildeY(tau), tildeY(tau_k))big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau(tildeY(tau) | c ) - nablalog q_T_g - tau_k(tildeY(tau_k) | c )\|^2big]\\ &le int_tau_k^tautilde f(u)E_tildeY(tau_k)big[\|nablalog q_T_g - tau_k(tildeY(tau_k) | c )\|^2big] + tilde g^2(u)E_tildeY(u)big[\|nabla^2log q_T_g - u(tildeY(u) | c)\|^2_Fbig]d u\\ &le int_tau_k^tautilde f(u)dsigma^-2_T_g - tau_k + tilde g^2(u)dsigma^-4_T_g - u - fracdd rbig(sigma_T - r^-4E_tildeY(r)sim q_T_g - r(cdot | c)[trace(boldsymbolSigma_T_g - r)]big)big|_r=u d u\\ &le int_tau_k^tautilde f(u)dsigma^-2_T_g - tau_k + tilde g^2(u)dsigma^-4_T_g - u d u \\ & + sigma_T - tau_k^-4E_Y(T_g - tau_k)[trace(boldsymbolSigma_T_g - tau_k)] - sigma_T - tau^-4E_Y(T_g - tau)[trace(boldsymbolSigma_T_g - tau)], where we omit to write out the dependency of boldsymbolSigma_tau on Y(tau) and c for simplicity. Finally, for the forward process Y in , since tildeY(tau) = Y(T_g - tau) for any tauin[0, T_g], we have for tau >0 and tauin[tau_k - 1, tau_k], &E_(Y(tau), Y(tau_k))big[\|nablalog q_tau(Y(tau) | c) - nablalog q_tau_k(Y(tau_k) | c ) \|^2big]\\ &le int_tau^tau_k f(s)dsigma^-2_tau_k + g^2(s)dsigma^-4_s d s + big(sigma_tau_k^-4E_Y(tau_k)[trace(boldsymbolSigma_tau_k)] - sigma_tau^-4E_Y(tau)[trace(boldsymbolSigma_tau)]big). This completes our proof.

For a given condition $\mathbf{c}$, recall the definition of $\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}), k_0(\mathbf{c})$ and $k_1$ in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma: score_discretization_error_bound} in Appendix \ref{sec: score_discretization_error}. By Lemma 14 and Lemma 21 of \cite{chen2023improved} and our Lemma \ref{lemma: score_function_norm_bound}, we can derive
\begin{align*}
    &\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}[g^2(\tau_k) - g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\\
    &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}(\Delta\tau)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\\
    &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{k_0(\mathbf{c}) - 1} \bigg[\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_\tau^{-1} \mathrm{d}\tau \bigg] + \int_{\tau_{k_0(\mathbf{c}) - 1}}^{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_\tau^{-1} \mathrm{d}\tau \\
    &\qquad + \int_{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{\tau_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot d\sigma^{-2}_\tau \mathrm{d}\tau + \sum_{k_0(\mathbf{c}) + 1}^K\bigg[\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot d\sigma^{-2}_\tau \mathrm{d}\tau\bigg]\\
    &\overset{\eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} }{\lesssim} \int_{0}^{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})} d(\Delta\tau)^2L(\mathbf{c})(1 + a\tau^2/4 + b\tau/2) \mathrm{d}\tau + \int_{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{\tau_{k_1}} \frac{d(\Delta\tau)^2}{a\tau^2/2 + b\tau} \mathrm{d}\tau + \int_{\tau_{k_1}}^{T_g} d(\Delta\tau)^2 \mathrm{d}\tau\\
    &\lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2L(\mathbf{c})\cdot \tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}) + d(\Delta\tau)^2\int_{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{\tau_{k_1}}\bigg(\frac{1}{\tau} + \frac{1}{\tau^2} \bigg)\mathrm{d}\tau + d(\Delta\tau)^2T_g\\
    &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipz_index_approximation}}{\lesssim} d(\Delta\tau)^2\bigg(L(\mathbf{c}) + 2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2 + \ln\big(2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2\big) + T_g \bigg)\\
    &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipschitz_constant}}{\lesssim} d(\Delta\tau)^2\bigg(L(\mathbf{c}) + T_g + 1 \bigg).
\end{align*}
Taking expectation on both sides w.r.t. $\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}[g^2(\tau_k) - g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\bigg]\\
    &\lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[L(\mathbf{c}) + T_g + 1\bigg]\\
    &\lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2[L_1 + T_g + 1].
\end{align*}
The proof is therefore complete.

Recall that $\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{Y}(0)\sim\mathcal{N}(\lambda_\tau\mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_\tau^2I_d)$. Using a similar argument as in the proof of Lemma 5 of \cite{bentonnearly}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{y}_\tau|\mathbf{c}) = -\sigma_\tau^{-2}I_d + \sigma_\tau^{-4}{\text{Cov}}_{q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big(\mathbf{y}(\tau) - \lambda_\tau\mathbf{Y}(0)\big) = -\sigma_\tau^{-2}I_d + \sigma_\tau^{-4}\lambda_\tau^2\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau.
\end{align*}
Noting that $\|A\|_F^2 = \text{trace}(A^TA)$ for a matrix $A$ and that $1 > \lambda_\tau^2 = \exp(-a\tau^2/2 - b\tau) = 2\sigma_\tau\dot\sigma_\tau/(a\tau + b)$, we can directly compute
\begin{align*}
    &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}_\tau|\mathbf{c})\|_F^2\big] \\
    &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^4\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\
    &\le d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\
    &\overset{\eqref{eq: posterior_cov_trace_dt}}{=} d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{2\sigma_\tau^{-7}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\sigma_\tau^3}{2\dot\sigma_\tau}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\
    &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{\sigma_\tau^{-4}}{a\tau + b}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau))}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\
    &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} + \frac{1}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\bigg(\sigma_\tau^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\bigg).
\end{align*}
The proof is complete by virtue of $g^2(\tau) = a\tau + b$.

    &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^4\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\
    &\le d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\

    &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{\sigma_\tau^{-4}}{a\tau + b}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau))}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\
    &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} + \frac{1}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\bigg(\sigma_\tau^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\bigg).
